market_holds: No option market (baseline). Spot $2.65 at the 18:08 UTC seal and $2.62 at the close per the Yahoo chart, -5.8% on the day after touching an intraday low of $2.425, at its 52-week low and 60% below the high. Run-up -8.9% over 5 days and -28.6% over 20 days, 20-day realised vol 85%, so one day's band is about 5.4%. The price round-tripped the October rally on EVX-01 three-year data: $2.83 on Oct 16, $4.05 close on Oct 20 (high $4.50 on Oct 21), -18% on Oct 26 after the Oct 23 ESMO release, and a drift down since. The supply overhang is now live: the EIB warrant-resale F-1/A went effective on Nov 13 (EFFECT plus 424B3 on EDGAR), covering 38.45M shares from the 2025 debt settlement, which the company says is not a capital raise. Guidance: cash of $14.0M at 2026-06-30 and runway 'into 2H27', repeated every quarter. No consensus worth the name (microcap with no revenue). Its own earnings days, close-to-close from my Yahoo bars: -10.3, +25.5, -5.9, +10.6, +9.3, -7.7, +4.1, so the median size is about 9% and four of seven were up. Opening gaps were smaller, -1.6% to +10%.
view: This is a cash-constrained AI-vaccine microcap. Its Q3 numbers (cash, burn) matter less than the narrative. The one new element is the framing: today's 6-K calls tomorrow's event a 'strategy and business update' (8:30 ET call), while every earlier quarter was a plain 'business update'. CEO Helen Tayton-Martin, ex-Adaptimmune and a partnering specialist, has been in the job almost a year. So a reset is likely: a reprioritised pipeline, a partnering-led model, possibly cost cuts or a runway change, possibly a deal. Its sign cannot be read in advance. A partnership, an MSD option exercise or a runway extension through cuts would gap a stock sitting at its lows up hard. A 'strategic alternatives' line, a shorter runway or a raise announced with the plan would push it down further, and the EIB resale shares have been sellable since Nov 13. Q3 cash should be about $10-11M if burn held near $4M a quarter and the August ATM ($1.5M) was all that was raised. I found no share-capital-increase announcement since August, which leaves the 2H27 runway claim plausible but tight. The stock has already sold off 35-40% from the October peak into the print, so a neutral update is cushioned. Even so, I cannot show that the price is wrong in either direction.

recommendation.reason: The decisive item, the content of the first 'strategy update', is unknowable from public sources before the release, and it could cut either way: a deal or runway extension against a reprioritisation, raise or strategic-alternatives line. The stock is oversold at its 52-week low with a fresh resale overhang, which argues against leaning short, but I have no dated evidence of a positive surprise. With no implied move and no consensus, there is no stale number to trade against.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A named partnership or MSD option exercise with upfront cash, or a runway extended past 2H27, would make it a clear up move. A raise or a strategic-alternatives review announced with the update would make it a clear down move.

self_critique: The case for a long: a stock at a fresh 52-week low, down about 40% from its October high, into a deliberately branded 'strategy update' from a deal-making CEO is set up for a relief gap. Companies rarely relabel an earnings call 'strategy' to deliver bad news without a cushion, and four of seven earnings days closed up. The case for a short: 'strategy update' at a near-cash microcap often means reprioritisation, cuts or a raise, and the EIB resale overhang caps any bounce. Both are plausible and neither is evidenced, so 50 stands.
